reasoning_quality_informational.v1_root_problem: Billing dispute tickets have doubled since August 2026, from a ~600/month baseline to 1180 (Aug) and 1260 (Sep) (E-03), while response times remain within SLA (E-02), ruling out a response-handling cause. The best-supported mechanism is a billing import/validation-rule defect introducing calculation errors during bill issuance (H-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE), evidenced by 59% of disputed bills carrying an accepted ACTUAL read rather than an ESTIMATED substitution (E-04), which weighs against AMI/field read failure being the majority driver.
reasoning_quality_informational.v2_root_problem: Billing dispute tickets surged from a ~600/month baseline to 1180 (Aug) and 1260 (Sep 2026) (E-03) because rule BV-17, deployed 2026-08-01, compares raw AMI register values to 12-month m3 history with unit_scaling=none (E-13); firmware v4.2 meters (rollout 2026-06) report readings in 0.1 m3 units (E-14), so their valid high-consumption reads are misflagged and rejected at import (REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION, 1184 of 1240 ESTIMATED-read disputed bills, 95.5%, E-12), forcing estimate substitution and wrong bills customers dispute.
reasoning_quality_informational.ideal_final_problem: BV-17 validation rejects valid firmware-v4.2 AMI reads (unit-scale mismatch on H-MDMS-BILL) and substitutes estimates.
